summary: <select> has no node in the accessibility tree, so an assistive user cannot see or operate the control at all - even though TASK-030 made it keyboard-operable.
evidence: BR-139. Measured while writing the BR-101 journey: the layout arena carries obj tag="select" id="sel", Session.AccessibilityTree() under the form returns only role=4 id="send"; cmd/goosie clickNode therefore cannot address a select (journey uses clickElementByID). Recorded in docs/tasks/TASK-030-SELECT-INTERACTION.md §9.4. Closed on 910c445 (feature 3c16f37). Oracles: test/engine/accessibility_test.go:TestAccessibilitySelectComboBoxAndOptions and :TestAccessibilitySelectTracksMoveSelect, both tagged // qc:BR-139, plus internal/platform/darwin/ax_role_test.go pinning the AppKit role codes. The integrator re-ran all five mutations on the branch and each one turned the feature off, then passed again on revert: emitter removed (combo missing), every option marked selected ("selected options = 3, want exactly 1"), combo value read from the select's value attribute ("combo value = \"\""), selectedness computed by index instead of the attribute ("Label:One ... want Two/two" after MoveSelect), and RoleComboBox mapped to GROUP ("maps to 1, want GOOSIE_AX_COMBO_BOX (12)"). cmd/goosie/journey_p1_forms_test.go:TestJourneySelectOptionChange now reaches the control through clickNode, i.e. through the accessibility tree, instead of clickElementByID. Disclosed: VoiceOver itself was never exercised - the darwin oracle asserts the role code, not what a screen reader says, so mutation (v) of the task spec has no behavioural test.

summary: ::first-line is not supported at all, so a first-line colour or weight is silently dropped. (The original attribution of selectors/03's three blank bands to missing ::first-letter/::first-line support is falsified - see evidence.)
evidence: BR-075. Registered by TASK-027 as 'the residual is the missing first-letter/first-line support'. Two of those three causes no longer hold, and one never did. (1) ::first-letter is implemented: 2f1519d 'feat(layout): implement ::first-letter pseudo-element drop cap box (BR-075)', merged 5978371. testdata/render-known-gaps.json declared selectors/03-pseudo-elements.png at 3 blank regions before that commit (git show 2f1519d^:testdata/render-known-gaps.json) and still declares 3; re-measured at 452b6c2 the same three bands remain, at the identical rows (457,475) (539,554) (579,599). Implementing ::first-letter removed none of them. (2) Those three bands are not missing content at all: Goosie paints the lines, ~20px away from Chromium's band rows, so the blank test fires on vertical drift. For band (457,475) Goosie has ink rows 437-455 and 483-498 and none in between, and the crop shows 'This paragraph has a checkmark after it' rendered with its checkmark. See GOOSIE-BLANKMETRIC-001. (3) What is genuinely unsupported is ::first-line, measured directly on 2026-10-26: a one-rule page 'p.fl::first-line{color:#ff0000;font-weight:bold}' at 400x200 renders 1,043 red px in Chromium (computed color rgb(255, 0, 0)) and 0 red px in Goosie, all 544 of its ink px black. Priority lowered P1 -> P2 on this measurement; the ::before/::after content in the same fixture renders, and the residual band count is an artifact of the metric, not of this defect.

summary: Colour emoji still draw as tofu: golang.org/x/image/font/opentype does not read sbix/COLR tables.
evidence: TASK-027 killed 8 of the 9 blank bands in unicode/02-emoji-symbols.png; the remaining band at rows (451,470) is Chromium's Apple Color Emoji line box (~26px) versus Goosie's 18px tofu line, i.e. cumulative vertical drift, not a missing glyph. Note added to docs/roadmap-v2.md. TASK-027 round 2 merged at 6074040: candidates are ordered by measured coverage, a face is admitted only when its cmap covers the rune, coverage is memoized per candidate path, and the 4 MiB ceiling is checked by os.Stat before ReadFile. Measured over whole ranges instead of samples: 364 non-CJK code points across 8 scripts, 358 resolve, and exactly 6 miss - U+03A2 (Greek), U+063B-U+063F (Arabic) - which the oracle now declares as gaps in both directions. CJK stays tofu on this host by admission design: every system CJK face is over the ceiling (Arial Unicode 22.2 MiB, STHeiti 55.7, Songti 66.9, PingFang ~50-80), so colour-emoji and CJK coverage remain the open half of this defect. The 6 Greek/Arabic code points are unrenderable by any admitted host face under the ceiling and are not tracked separately.

summary: TestNativeEndToEndPlaysARealVideo is load-sensitive: under a busy machine it can time out, which risks a false red in the sweep's gate step.
evidence: test/engine/media_native_test.go:264. Observed while running full suites in parallel worktrees; TASK-029 §3 forbids raising the timeout as a fix, so it is recorded here instead. Same class observed on 2026-10-25 at 20:07: TestFootprintAtRestIsBoundedByConfiguredCaches reported retained=257.03 MiB against configured=207.10 MiB while 14 orphaned busy-loop shells from an old stress command held the 1-minute load average near 90; the identical run passed at 2.29s on the same commit (130bc9a) once the load was removed. The at-rest footprint criterion is therefore load-sensitive and must be measured on an idle machine, never in parallel with another suite.

summary: Button-level formnovalidate is not honoured: a submit button carrying formnovalidate still runs constraint validation, so the 'Send without saving' pattern cannot submit an incomplete form.
evidence: grep -rn formnovalidate internal/engine returns no matches, while the merged bypass oracle test/engine/form_submission_test.go:TestFormNovalidateBypass only exercises the form-level novalidate attribute. summary: Browser-level tests read the layout arena from the test goroutine, so the journeys that decide whether a feature works are unsynchronised against the engine's input goroutine.
evidence: 14 sites in cmd/goosie/*_test.go walk sess.Arena.Objects directly (cmd/goosie/e2e_test.go:188 clickElementByID, clipboard_test.go:36,121, form_nav_test.go:58,130,251, ...). TASK-030's -race run proved the same class of cross-goroutine DOM read is unsafe, and the locking contract requires locked Session accessors. A mutation that rebuilds layout can therefore produce a torn read or an unsynchronised click coordinate instead of a clean failure.

summary: The tab scroll-restore journey asserts a cross-tab inequality instead of an exact offset, so it can pass for the wrong reason or fail when both tabs clamp to the same scroll extent.
evidence: cmd/goosie/journey_p1_tabs_test.go:96-105 presses PageDown twice in tab 2 and waits for active.ScrollY() > tab1Scroll, comparing one tab's offset against a different tab's; the same test then asserts exact equality (== tab1Scroll, == tab2Scroll) at lines 121 and 132. The inequality oracle depends on page heights and clamp values, and it is the assertion that failed twice under machine load.

summary: 103 of the 161 P0/P1 QA cases still have no tagged test, so most of the manual catalogue remains unverified automatically even though every P0 case is now tagged.
evidence: test/qc/traceability.golden.json at 910c445: 185 cases, P0 19/19 tagged, P0+P1 161 cases of which 58 tagged, so 103 P1 cases have no tagged test. summary: The parity harness can report success while its own evidence shrinks: --no-strict deletes fixtures from the denominator, and the known-gaps baseline is an upper bound (<=), so inflating it hides blank bands instead of exposing them.
evidence: BR-176/BR-177. Measured by importing testdata/parity.py (importlib) against a one-fixture temp corpus, leaving the real /tmp render dirs untouched: declared baseline 5 with 0 measured blank bands yields ('a.png', 'PASS', 100.0, [], 5, None); deleting the chromium render under strict=False yields [] - the fixture vanishes from the report, so N/N (100%) and rc 0. strict=True does report MISSING ('chromium render missing') and a missing gaps file raises FileNotFoundError, so the fail-closed half exists; what is missing is any floor on the number of scored fixtures and any check that a declared band baseline still equals what is measured. grep shows no script, Makefile or CI target passes --no-strict, and every entry in testdata/render-known-gaps.json currently matches its measured band count exactly (2/2, 1/1, 3/3, 1/1, 3/3 at 4437f65), so an equality gate is satisfiable today. CLOSED 2026-10-26 by 62fd38c, integration 5d2fff4, merge e310f55. --no-strict is deleted from argparse, so the flag is unrecognised rather than merely unused: test/gatecheck/parity_harness_test.go:TestParityRejectsNoStrictFlag asserts a non-zero exit and the argparse 'unrecognized' text, and `strict` is gone from score_fixtures' signature, so all three missing-render branches append a FixtureResult unconditionally. The baseline is now an exact ratchet (`elif len(blank_rows) != allowed_blanks` -> FAIL with 'known-gap baseline is stale: declared N, measured M'), and the denominator has a floor: len(results) < MIN_SCORED_FIXTURES returns 2. Oracles: testdata/parity_selftest.py (5 cases over a temp corpus, no browser, no network, never touches /tmp/{goosie,playwright}-renders), driven by TestParitySelftestIsGreen; TestParityFixtureFloorMatchesCorpus reads the floor out of parity.py with a regex so the two numbers cannot drift. Tagged BR-176 (1 test) and BR-177 (2 tests); golden re-synced and both rows flipped NOT RUN -> PASS. Five mutation proofs in TASK-036 §7.3 plus one at integration: setting the floor to 999 gives 'testdata/render has 81 HTML fixtures, below MIN_SCORED_FIXTURES 999' -> FAIL, so the floor still polices shrinkage. Two things the integrator changed and one limit kept visible: (1) the branch's Go test pinned `count == floor`, which reddened main the moment TASK-041 added a fixture - i.e. it punished growing the corpus - so the comparison is now `count < floor` and the floor rose 80 -> 81; (2) proof (v) (dropping --strict from argparse) kills NO test, because no test passes the flag; it is defended only by the call site scripts/run-parity.sh:146, which is why --strict was kept as a no-op instead of being removed too; (3) the equality ratchet makes testdata/render-known-gaps.json a per-host baseline - see GOOSIE-CIPARITY-001.

summary: A select's submitted value is raw option text content and the first selected option wins, so Goosie sends whitespace the server never sees from Chromium and resolves multi-selected markup to the wrong option.
evidence:
BR-101/BR-104/BR-106/BR-139. Measured on this host: Goosie submitted name="c" value="
  Charcoal
" for an option whose text content is '
  Charcoal
' and encoded it as c=%0A++Charcoal%0A, while Chromium/Playwright normalises the same shape to option.textContent = '  Hi
  there
' -> option.value === 'Hi there' (strip plus internal whitespace collapse). For a <select> with two selected options Chromium reports selectedIndex 1, value 'b', formdata 'b' (last wins) whereas SelectedOption (internal/engine/focus.go:634) returns the first. The accessibility tree trims option labels (internal/engine/accessibility.go:172) but the combo Value comes from controlValue untrimmed, so one control announces a different string than it submits. All four blocked cases already have tagged tests that pass today (BR-101 7 tests, BR-104/BR-106 one journey each, BR-139 3 tests) - none asserts the normalised value or the tie-break, so this defect hides behind green tests, not behind a missing test. Optgroup is out of scope: internal/engine/select.go:46-48 records that options nested in an optgroup are unreachable.

summary: Seven P1 chrome/session cases (BR-043/044/045/049/054/055/056) had no tagged test at all, so visit-log ordering, forward-trail discard, session cursor restore and private-mode isolation were trusted entirely to manual QC.
evidence: test/qc/traceability.golden.json at 4437f65 lists tests: null for all seven. d61403d (merged at f53be0c) tags one oracle per case. Integrator re-ran everything rather than trusting the report: go test -count=1 ./... FULL-RC=0 including test/gate and test/gatecheck; -race on cmd/goosie, test/tabs, test/history rc 0; go vet -all ./... rc 0; go test ./test/qc/ -update followed by empty git diff (golden idempotent, and still idempotent after the merge). Seven behaviour-off mutations were reproduced by hand, each killing its own test: consecutive-repeat guard (Entries() = 2 records, want 1), Push forward-truncation ([a b c d]@3, want [a b d]@2), private opening profile stores (private app stores/client = ... want client and no profile stores), private journalling (session_active.json exists after close plus regular startup found a private crash journal containing https://private.example/secret), private jar not cleared (private jar after Close = [{Name:Y ...}]), failed load recorded (history after failed load has 4 entries, want 3), and dropped history cursor (5 assertions red in TestSessionStateRoundTrip). All reverted; git status clean and no MUTATION-TEMP residue. An extra integrator probe found the per-tab incognito case is already pinned: dropping the !tab.Incognito() guard at cmd/goosie/navigation.go:319 fails the pre-existing TestIncognitoHistorySuppression. Disclosed limits: one oracle per case, and the failed-load fixture uses a connection-refused URL rather than an HTTP 500 page, so the error-page branch of that rule is untested.

summary: On nine real web pages Goosie lays out nothing, or paints a handful of pixels, and still exits 0 with an empty stderr - the user gets a blank window and the engine records no reason anywhere.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-001. Measured by testdata/live-parity.py against Chromium/Playwright at viewport 1280x1024, dpr 1, wait_until=load, screenshots viewport-only on both sides. Source: docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1656Z-4de0fca5.json (94 of 100 pages comparable). Eight pages have doc_height=0 AND ink_goosie=0 with goosie_rc=0 and an empty goosie_diag: apnews.com (Chromium painted 15,805 ink px), www.nytimes.com (68,129), www.japantimes.co.jp (17,749), www.reuters.com (13,145), www.etsy.com (16,539), www.newegg.com (17,467), www.zara.com (8,846), www.gov.vn (501,735). vnexpress.net is a different shape of the same silence: doc_height=691 but ink_goosie=32 against ink_chromium=301,440. All nine carry the identical label in the earlier run (2026-10-25T1630Z) as well, so this is not load noise; of the 6 label changes between the runs none is in this family (www.usatoday.com was LAYOUT_EMPTY at run 1 and LOW_COVERAGE at run 2, so it is deliberately not counted here). Offline probes on saved copies of the served HTML prove this is at least two distinct causes, not one: www.gov.vn reproduces with no network (curl-saved 192,815-byte document whose decoded text carries 11,859 visible characters across 177,201 body characters, served with 26 inline <script> tags) and ./bin/goosie -screenshot on that file yields rc 0, ink 0, while -gate -frames 120 reports doc_height=0, tiles_rasterized=0, zero_work_frames=120 - the frame path ran 120 frames with no document to draw. apnews.com does NOT reproduce offline: the same command on its saved 2,610,822-byte copy (70,685 visible characters) paints 763,855 ink px at doc_height=34,867, so the live failure of that page must come from the fetch/response path rather than from layout of the markup. (www.gov.vn is also the only page in this family whose corpus expect is 'static'; the other seven are 'js-revealed'.) Caveat for whoever investigates: style_passes and layout_passes read 0 on both runs, including on apnews where layout clearly succeeded, so those two counters are frame-window figures and must not be cited as evidence that styling never ran. Nothing distinguishes any of these from a page that genuinely has nothing to draw: the -screenshot path exits 0, so neither CI nor a user can tell. Not root-caused further - TASK-038 §4 forbids engine changes in a measurement task. TASK-039 SPLIT (measured 2026-10-26, docs/tasks/TASK-039-LIVE-PAGE-NO-OUTPUT.md §5.7): the family is six branches, not one. Three now have fixes on main - the refusal status line (branch A: a source that answers 4xx used to be painted as an ordinary page with no note), `nodeType` in the JS binding (branch B: a Sizzle-shaped `9 === doc.nodeType` gate that never passed, so the setup script died before revealing content; oracle BR-188), and uncaught-exception recording (branch E: BR-189/BR-190, so a page that broke now says so on stderr). Three stay open: branch C (missing Node/DOM APIs - `createDocumentFragment`/`insertBefore` completion), branch D (paced modes never install `setTick`, so `PumpJS` never runs and JS-revealed content cannot appear in a `-screenshot`/`-gate`/`-bench` run), and branch F (the corner ink artefact, GOOSIE-LIVE-006). The comparable-page count did not rise, so this defect stays open. One page in the family did move: vnexpress.net went from ink_goosie=32 (BLANK_OUTPUT) to 320,348 (LOW_COVERAGE) between the da68c5b and eef92ae sweeps - attributed offline on one saved copy to the CSS string-state fix, see GOOSIE-CSSSTRING-002, and NOT to any TASK-039 branch. CORRECTION (2026-10-26, integrator): the vnexpress.net movement from ink_goosie=32 to 320,348 between the da68c5b and eef92ae sweeps is real, but the sentence appended above attributing it to 'the CSS string-state fix repaired the sheet' is falsified by a direct measurement - see GOOSIE-CSSSTRING-003: on vnexpress's own second inline stylesheet the eef92ae parser loses a tail rule that da68c5b keeps (marker ink 0 vs 14,400). The page-level improvement therefore comes from a different sheet on the page, and the branch is still open for this site (LOW_COVERAGE, coverage 0.441).

summary: A legal custom property name that begins with digits (--8e8e8e) is mistaken for an oversized geometry dimension, so the whole document is refused: cafef.vn gets no window, and the message names no property, no value and no limit.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-002. Reproduced offline with no network from a saved copy: ./bin/goosie -screenshot -url file:///tmp/cafef.html (217,170 bytes) exits 1 and writes exactly one stderr line, 'goosie: goosie: build session: CSS numeric value outside safe geometry range' (the prefix is doubled). The live sweep labels it ADMISSION_CAPPED in docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1656Z-4de0fca5.json; in the earlier run it was GOOSIE_CRASH, the same family mislabelled before the ladder put a refusal check ahead of the exit-code check. ROOT CAUSE, measured by bisection and not yet fixed: document -> 9 <style> blocks (dropping them clears the refusal; dropping style= attributes does not) -> block 8 of 36 rules -> one rule, '.box-ttdn .list .mdn .time { color: var(--8e8e8e, #8e8e8e); ... }'. The one-line repro is ':root{--8e8e8e:#8e8e8e}' and '.a{color:var(--8e8e8e)}'. The name of that custom property begins with digits, so the tokenizer reads 8e8 as a scientific number and then swallows the following 'e8' as a unit, producing a Dimension token worth 800,000,000; internal/engine/limits.go:239-241 applies MaxGeometry = 2<<20 (2,097,152) to dimensions and percentages, and the document is refused. A variant matrix measured on this host confirms the mechanism exactly: ':root{--8e8:1}' rc 0 (plain number, cap deliberately skipped), ':root{--8e8e8:1}' rc 1, ':root{--1e9e9:1}' rc 1, ':root{--8e5e5:1}' rc 0 (800,000 under the cap), ':root{--1e2e2:1}' rc 0, ':root{--abc8e8e8:1}' rc 0 (ident, no number token), '.a{width:8e8}' rc 0, '.a{width:8e8e8px}' rc 1 (a genuine dimension, correctly refused). Chromium, measured with Playwright on the same minimal document, resolves var(--8e8e8e) to rgb(171, 205, 239): a custom property name that begins with digits is legal and contains no number at all, so this refusal is a false positive that blanks an entire news site - renaming the one ident to --grey makes the saved cafef document render at rc 0 with 554,999 ink pixels. Hypotheses already disproved on this document: replacing every 7-or-more-digit number (including z-index:999999999) does not clear the refusal, because the trigger is an 8-character ident with no run of digits; and the document loads no external stylesheet, so linked CSS is not involved. Compounding the damage, the same coarse message is emitted from three sites - internal/engine/limits.go:226 (float64 overflow), :231 (non-finite), :241 (magnitude) - and none names the property, the value, or the bound, unlike :249 'CSS declaration limit exceeded (%d)'.

summary: A -screenshot run that gave up at its hard-coded 25 s deadline is indistinguishable from one that settled: same exit code, same PNG, no field that says 'not settled'.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-003. cmd/goosie/drive.go:170 sets steadyDriver's deadline to 25 * time.Second, and :241 ends the wait with 'if d.settledFn == nil || time.Since(started) >= d.deadline' - returning as though the run had completed. Nothing marks the difference: no stderr, nonzero exit, or field in the artifact. Measured headroom on the 2026-10-25 corpus: the slowest Goosie render was 8.93 s (www.straitstimes.com), then 7.70 s (www.noaa.gov) and 6.66 s (dw.com), so no page in this sweep reached the deadline - the gap is unexercised here, not proven harmless. The harness had to work around it by timing each render itself and inventing a NOT_SETTLED label (testdata/live-parity.py classify, selftest case 'slow'); any other consumer of -screenshot has no such signal. Changing the constant is out of scope for a measurement task (TASK-038 §4), which is why it is registered rather than tuned.

summary: The parity scorer can grade a page 'OK' while Goosie's ink sits almost nowhere near Chromium's: coverage is an ink-mass ratio that rises above 1, and the positional score (worst_iou) is recorded but never consulted.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-004 - a defect in the measuring infrastructure, not in the engine. coverage comes from parity.score_regions (testdata/parity.py:279): goosie_total / chromium_total, so it exceeds 1 whenever Goosie paints more ink than the reference. 30 of the 94 comparable pages in docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1656Z-4de0fca5.json report coverage > 1.0, up to 2.83 (www.w3.org/Style/CSS/, 1,306,325 Goosie ink px vs 15,209 Chromium), 2.57 (ebay.com, 1,228,884 vs 94,816), 2.32 (validator.w3.org). Worse, the label ignores position: among the 46 OK pages, 26 have worst_iou < 0.5 and 16 have worst_iou < 0.1, including en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam (coverage 1.547, worst_iou 0.001, 0 of 4 bands blank) and wiki/Cuneiform (1.972, 0.014). grep of testdata/live-parity.py shows worst_iou is written at :162 and never read by classify. Written on 2026-10-25 as: 'blank-band and dimension checks are position-sensitive, so LAYOUT_EMPTY, BLANK_OUTPUT, MISSING_REGIONS and DIMENSION_MISMATCH stay trustworthy'. That half is now falsified for BLANK_OUTPUT: measured on 2026-10-26 at 452b6c2, a band reported blank can hold Goosie's line ~20px away (GOOSIE-BLANKMETRIC-001), so BLANK_OUTPUT does not by itself prove content is absent. LAYOUT_EMPTY, MISSING_REGIONS and DIMENSION_MISMATCH are unaffected by that measurement and still stand. What is missing is a positional criterion that separates 'content absent' from 'content elsewhere'. Disclosed rather than retuned: LIVE_COVERAGE_OK = 0.60 and MIN_SCORED = 75 were fixed before the first run and never adjusted afterwards (TASK-038 §6.5).

summary: The CSS parser's quote-tracking scanners never end an unterminated string at a newline, so Goosie swallows the rest of the sheet and paints it on the page as generated content.
The ::first-letter admission rule is written three times and the incremental-restyle copy has no oracle: gutting it leaves the whole suite green.
evidence: Three copies of one rule. internal/style/pseudo.go:37-56 (resolvePseudoElements) and internal/style/pseudo.go:91-105 (reResolvePseudoSubtree) carry the identical 'before/after/first-letter' loop and the identical 'cs.Content != "" && cs.Content != "none"' admission test; the third decision is in internal/layout/arena.go:498-512. The re-resolve copy has none of the comment that explains the first one (pseudo.go:47-51, why content:"" must still generate a box for clearfixes), so whoever edits one copy will not know why the other exists. reResolvePseudoSubtree is reachable only from internal/style/incremental.go:157, i.e. the hover/restyle path. No oracle covers it: test/layout/first_letter_test.go:246 TestFirstLetterIncremental asserts only WorkCounts().LayoutBuilds deltas (:279 must not change, :295 must change by 1) - that a rebuild happened, never what style or box the rebuilt first-letter got. Measured at 452b6c2: replacing the first-letter branch inside the reResolvePseudoSubtree copy so it admits nothing left go test ./... green (mutation M2 survived), which also breaks the [R-7] rule that every oracle needs a positive expectation. Not a user-visible defect today - the copies agree - so P2: it is an uncovered-code and silent-divergence risk on the path users reach by hovering.

summary: A global inline-layout float skip shipped inside the ::first-letter commit changes float layout on real pages, is not needed by that feature, and no test fails when it is removed.
evidence: internal/layout/inline.go:387 - 'if k.Node == nil || k.Style == nil || k.Style.Display == style.DisplayNone || k.Style.Float != style.FloatNone' sits in inlineInto's generic child loop, so it drops every floated child from inline collection everywhere. git blame: the clause is from 2f1519db (2026-10-25, the ::first-letter commit); the rest of the line is db4bedff (2026-09-17). It is not first-letter specific and the feature does not need it. Scope measured 2026-10-26 at 452b6c2 by deleting the clause, rebuilding, and re-rendering all 80 corpus fixtures at 800x2400 with both binaries: exactly one fixture differs - layout-features/05-floats.png, 51,447 px of symmetric ink difference - and the other 79 are pixel-identical. At the scored 800x600 viewport the same change is 162 px and the fixture passes either way, so make parity cannot see it at all. On that fixture at 800x2400 the parity numbers flip hard: worst_iou 0.6866 -> 0.0000, coverage 0.9813 -> 0.9474, blank bands 0 -> 1 (Chromium band rows 1055-1071 cols 20-460 holds 2,775 ink px; Goosie holds 0 with the clause and 2,289 without). Those numbers do not prove the clause is wrong: the line 'Content after the overflow:hidden container (should be below).' is painted in both variants, about 15px apart, so the band goes blank from vertical drift (GOOSIE-BLANKMETRIC-001), not from lost content. What is proven is that it is uncovered: removing it failed no test in go test ./... (mutation M3 survived). Decision owed by the owner: either add a float test that fails without the clause and say which spec rule it implements, or drop it from the feature and land it separately with that test.

summary: A 'blank band' in the parity metric can mean 'Goosie painted that line 20px away', not 'content missing', so the known-gaps baseline counts and TASK-027's band classification are not evidence about features.
evidence: testdata/parity.py:253-279 score_regions(): bands come from content_bands(cm) on the Chromium mask only, and a band is reported blank when goosie_count == 0 inside Chromium's exact rows. The IoU path dilates by one row (_dilate_one) before comparing; the blank test does not dilate at all, so a line that is present but shifted by more than the band's own gap registers as absent. Two measured instances on 2026-10-26 at 452b6c2. selectors/03-pseudo-elements band (457,475): Goosie has ink rows 437-455 and 483-498 and none between, and the crop shows the paragraph and its checkmark painted. layout-features/05-floats band (1055,1071): both the current build and a build with the float skip removed paint the sentence, about 15px apart, yet one reports 0 ink in the band and the other 2,289. Blast radius: testdata/render-known-gaps.json stores 5 fixtures / 10 bands and is the release-gate baseline; docs/tasks/TASK-027-GLYPH-COVERAGE.md 6 classified those bands by cause, and at least three of them are now known to be artifacts; testdata/live-parity.py imports score_regions by reference, so every live row inherits the same meaning of BLANK_OUTPUT. Fix direction, without touching any threshold: report a drift-adjusted blank - search Goosie ink in a window of +-band height around the Chromium rows and label 'shifted' separately from 'absent' - then re-classify the 10 declared bands from the new column. LIVE_COVERAGE_OK, PASS_AT, THRESHOLD and MIN_INK stay frozen; this adds a signal, it does not loosen one. MERGED STATE, re-measured by the integrator on 2026-10-26 at fc15c19 rather than taken from the branch: score_regions_drift landed as a report-only second view; scoring the SAME 82 renders with main and with the branch produced ZERO field differences across all 82 fixtures (match_pct, status, blank_regions, blank_region_rows, coverage_ratio, worst_region_iou) and the summary stayed 82/82 at average 96.088% with known gaps 5 fixtures / 10 bands. On the corpus the split is 10 declared blank bands -> 9 shifted, 1 truly_blank (html-features/01-forms-complete.png rows 593-599: zero ink inside the +-7 window, nearest ink 8 rows away). Three mutations were run and reverted here, not quoted: drift window = 0 reddens the selftest case that expects a shifted band, window x40 reddens case D3 (ink painted 100 rows away) so the width is load-bearing rather than tuned, and redefining the OLD signal inside score_regions - instead of adding a side result - makes `make parity` exit 1 on the known-gap equality. render-known-gaps.json is deliberately NOT re-baselined to 1: blank_regions keeps its original meaning, so declaring one band would loosen the gate under cover of a reclassification. BR-187 carries the oracle (test/gatecheck/parity_harness_test.go:TestParityDriftMetricIsGreen plus selftest cases D1-D4); the ratchet was re-measured, not assumed: P0 tagged 19, P0/P1 tagged 69, unchanged, because BR-187 is P2. WHAT STILL KEEPS THIS OPEN: the drift column exists only for the fixture corpus. The live sweep's 25 MISSING_REGIONS rows are still graded by the un-adjusted band count, and TASK-042 could not measure their drift share because live-parity.py writes its PNGs into a temp dir and shutil.rmtree removes them when it exits (live-parity.py:679,688) - so the number everyone will ask for, 'how many of the 25 are displacement', is still unknown, and the sweep's own label for a whole-page blank (BLANK_OUTPUT, 1 page, vnexpress at 32 ink px) is structurally NOT drift: with page-wide ink below LIVE_MIN_INK no band can reach MIN_INK in any window. MEASURED ON THE LIVE SIDE (2026-10-26, docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1920Z-eef92ae7.json): en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat is labelled MISSING_REGIONS with 1 blank band at rows [98,119] while Goosie's total ink is 215,401 against Chromium's 216,818 - 0.65% less, over a 23,269 px document. A page that paints 99.35% of the reference's ink and is called 'missing regions' is exactly the confusion this defect is about, and live-parity.py cannot yet separate shifted from truly blank because it deletes both PNGs after scoring (testdata/live-parity.py:679,688). The parity-side split is shipped (BR-187); the live-side split is the remaining half.

summary: Render parity is only ever measured on one host: the CI parity job on ubuntu-latest fails 14 of 80 fixtures while this macOS host scores 81 of 81, so a green `make parity` is evidence about a machine, not about the engine.
evidence: Discovered while closing GOOSIE-PARITYGATE-001, from CI's own artifact, not from a local run. The last three CI runs of the job 'Render parity vs Chromium' all concluded failure: 39990406790 (2026-10-23), 40069270435 and 40107385303 (2026-10-24). Newest artifact (run 40107385303, job 120911782700, head c8cd80b, ubuntu-latest, playwright==1.49.1): summary total 80, passing 66, failing 14, errors 0, avg_match_pct 93.638 at threshold 30 / pass_at 90.0. Same corpus on this macOS host at e310f55: 81/81 passing, avg 96.09%. The 14 CI failures are html-features/02 89.9, typography/09 89.62, overflow/01 89.28, typography/06 88.78, layout-features/01 88.76, typography/04 88.65, edge-cases/02 88.37, colors/02 87.19, tables/03 87.08, edge-cases/01 87.08, tables/02 86.39, positioning/03 83.95, selectors/01 81.64, colors/01 80.33. Two structural readings of that list, both measured: 0 dimension mismatches across all 80 rows (goosie_size == chromium_size in every row), so the pages are comparable shapes and the disagreement is pixels only; and the CI pass band starts at 90.364 while the worst failure is 89.9 - the verdict for 17% of the corpus sits within 0.46 points of the pass line, i.e. the gate is a cliff, not a slope. Hypothesis, NOT tested: Linux font rasterisation shifts text enough to move those 14 rows under PASS_AT, because no same-commit A/B exists - CI has never run at the current head and this host never scored c8cd80b. Why it must not be waved away: TASK-036 turned the known-gaps baseline into an exact ratchet, so render-known-gaps.json (5 fixtures / 10 bands) is now host-specific, and on another host a shifted band becomes 'known-gap baseline is stale' FAIL rather than a silent pass; whether that actually bites on Linux is unknowable from the artifact, because per-region scoring did not exist at c8cd80b (grep -c blank_regions on that revision's parity.py = 0) and the report therefore carries no iou, coverage or band columns at all. Needed, in order: one ubuntu-latest run of the current head with --render --render-chromium, its parity.json archived; then either a per-platform baseline file or a recorded decision that Linux CI is the authority for this gate; then re-examine whether a 90.0 pass_at is defensible when the host spread alone can cross it. Separately, the same run's 'Race detector' job also failed, so BR-179's 'go test ./..., go vet, archtest and the gate suite all exit 0 on the candidate commit' is currently unmet on CI for reasons unrelated to parity - unmeasured here, since the failure log for that job was not pulled. CORRECTION to 'needs a Linux host': module-graph questions ARE measurable on this machine via GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go list (that is how GOOSIE-LICENSE-001 was proven), but PIXEL questions are not - no container runtime exists here (docker, podman, colima all absent), so the 14 CI failures cannot be reproduced or dismissed locally, and the only route to a Linux render is a CI run, which needs a push the user has not authorised.

summary: The distribution-provenance gate cannot pass on both build targets: golang.org/x/sys is linked only on Linux, and the allowlist is checked in both directions, so pinning it reddens macOS while leaving it unpinned reddens CI.
evidence: Gate 8 (test/gatecheck/licenses_test.go TestLinkedDependenciesPinned) is the only evidence for the licence provenance of the shipped binaries, and it enforces two directions: every linked module must be pinned (:70) and every pinned module must be linked (:78-82). go list -deps is target-dependent, so the two directions contradict each other across platforms and NO allowlist content can satisfy both. Measured at 32e3409 on this darwin/arm64 host without any Linux machine, because GOOS/GOARCH are honoured by go list: `go list -f '{{if not .Standard}}{{.Module.Path}}@{{.Module.Version}}{{end}}' -deps ./cmd/goosie ./cmd/goosie-headless | sort -u` yields 7 modules (regexp2/v2 v2.5.2, goja, sourcemap, pprof, x/image v0.45.0, x/net v0.60.0, x/text v0.42.0) with no x/sys, while the same command under GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 yields 8, adding golang.org/x/sys@v0.48.0 (chain: go mod why -m golang.org/x/sys -> x/image/font/opentype -> x/image/vector -> x/sys/cpu; x/image/vector IS linked on darwin too - grep -c gives 1 - so the delta is precisely the x/sys/cpu leaf). Both directions of the trap were run, not inferred: CI's own log for run 40107385303 job 120911782481 at head c8cd80b says 'licenses_test.go:71: linked module golang.org/x/sys@v0.48.0 is not in dependency-licenses.txt (re-audit and amend)' and that is the ONLY test failure in that job (no DATA RACE line anywhere in it, so the job title is misleading), while appending exactly that line here and re-running produced 'licenses_test.go:80: allowlist entry golang.org/x/sys@v0.48.0 is linked into no release binary (stale pin?)' -> FAIL, after which the file was restored and the test went ok again. Consequence for the release DoD: BR-179 ('go test ./..., go vet -all ./..., archtest and the gate suite all exit 0 on the candidate commit') is unmet on CI for this single cause, and it has been unmet for the last three runs (39990406790, 40069270435, 40107385303). The licence itself is not the problem: /Users/vyquocvu/go/pkg/mod/golang.org/x/sys@v0.48.0/LICENSE is the standard Go BSD-3-Clause text (Copyright 2009 The Go Authors; three conditions including the no-endorsement clause; ALL WARRANTIES disclaimer), already inside the permitted set, and the directory's PATENTS file is golang's standard grant, not copyleft. What is owed is a target-aware contract: declare the release target list in code, pin the union of modules across those targets, and judge staleness only against modules absent from EVERY target - plus a table-driven oracle so this fails on any laptop before CI does. TASK-043 §2 leaves one thing unmeasured on purpose: whether a third target (windows, linux/arm64) pulls yet another module.

summary: The TASK-041 bad-string fix treated every newline inside a quoted CSS string as the line break that ends it, including an escaped one (`\` + newline), so real stylesheets that split a long quoted value across two lines lost that declaration AND the rest of the sheet: doc.rust-lang.org/std/ dropped from 95,783 ink px to 53,215. No committed gate could see it.
evidence: Mechanism: f5cec79 (the commit that closed GOOSIE-CSSSTRING-001) added `closesStringAt(quote, c) { return c == quote || c == '\n' }` and wired it into three scanners - parseRule's selector loop, parseRule's declaration-body loop, and parseBlockWithRules' statement loop - with no handling of the backslash that escapes the next byte. CSS Syntax L3 4.3.7 makes a RAW newline end an open string as a bad-string, but 4.3.8 makes `\` + newline a valid escape *inside* the token. rustdoc's generated CSS ends five lines (6/54/61/65/68 of its main sheet) with `\` inside `url("data:image/svg+xml,…")`, so Goosie cut the string, ate the `;`, dropped the declaration, and lost every rule after it in that sheet. Ground truth measured on Chromium/Playwright 131.x on this host, four shapes, all in TASK-041 §7.1: escaped `url()` keeps 2 rules with `background-image` computed to `url("data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='a'%3E%3C/svg%3E")` and the image loading; escaped `font-family` computes to `GoosieSerif`; a RAW newline keeps 1 rule with 0 declarations and computed colour black; an escaped newline in an attribute selector yields 2 rules with selectorText `a[title="xy"]` and the following `.z` still applying. Pre-fix Goosie scored 0 declarations, 0 declarations, 0 declarations (already correct) and 1 merged rule respectively. Real-page effect, same canvas 1280x1024 dpr 1, metric parity.ink_mask: 4de0fca 95,783 px / 23 content bands, da68c5b (TASK-041 merged) 53,215 px / 16 bands, after the fix 95,814 px / 23 bands. On the minimal probe /tmp/escprobe/escaped-newline.html at 800x600 the fixed build's PNG is md5-identical to the 4de0fca PNG (c47c831b9f4889fa31eaa3ca127364f9) - green 40,000 / red 40,000 px vs the regression's 0 / 0 / 445 ink. WHY NO GATE SAW IT, which is the part worth keeping: `make parity` reported 81/81 passing at average 96.09% both before and after the regression shipped, because no fixture in testdata/render contained an escaped newline; the unit oracle in test/css covered four raw-newline shapes and no backslash; and a SAVED copy of the same rustdoc page renders identically on both binaries (51,939 px / 17 bands) because the escaped CSS only arrives on a fresh fetch - so the offline A/B that validated TASK-041 was blind by construction. The only thing that caught it was the 100-site live sweep (docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1845Z-da68c5bc.json), which is evidence for the sweep being a gate and not a report. Fixed in a9f6218: the three scanners skip the byte after a backslash while a string is open, and stripEscapedNewlines removes `\` + line-break pairs from inside quoted values the way Chromium computes them, leaving `\2014`, `\A` and Windows paths untouched. Proofs measured: (M1) reverting internal/css/parser.go makes the new fixture css-features/09-escaped-newline-string.html score 84.87% FAIL with blank_regions 2/0 rows [(295,310),(425,452)], 81/82 passing, parity exit 1; (M2) deleting only the stripEscapedNewlines call reddens exactly one assertion - and the fixture stays green at 96.24%, so the value-unescape half is guarded by the unit oracle ONLY, stated plainly rather than assumed; (M3) the raw-newline control branch of TestEscapedNewlineVersusRawNewline was green before the fix and stays green after it, so nothing was loosened. Still open in this family, recorded not hidden: escaped QUOTES (`content:"a\"b"`) still close the string at the five scanners this change did not touch (parser.go :1321, :1346, :1419, :1681, :1784 and SplitDeclarations), which is the same debt §6 of TASK-041 already logged for stripComments and readString; and Goosie keeps the escape pair verbatim in selector text (`a[title="x\<NL>y"]`) where Chromium serialises `a[title="xy"]`. BR-186 now carries 9 tests and its measured row names both defects.

summary: A Content-Type sent with a comma instead of a semicolon (`text/html, charset=UTF-8`) is not recognised as a displayable type, so Goosie treats the response as a download: the page never paints and -screenshot exits 1 with no PNG while Chromium renders the same bytes.
evidence: Found by the 100-site live sweep at da68c5b, on https://www.target.com/s/coffee (label changed OK -> FETCH_FAILED-class, then proven to be neither network nor a Goosie regression). Root cause: internal/download/download.go:21 ShouldDownload strips parameters with `strings.IndexByte(ct, ';')` only, so the header value `text/html, charset=UTF-8` lowercases to `text/html, charset=utf-8`, matches none of the four whitelisted cases, and falls through to `default: return true` - download it. RFC 9110 §8.3 puts parameters after `;`, so the comma form is a server-side bug, but a browser is the party that has to cope and Chromium does. Measured offline, not argued: /tmp/ctprobe/serve.py replays the exact response bytes the site sends (429 status, `Content-Type: text/html, charset=UTF-8`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, the challenge body); against that single server Goosie exits 1 and writes no PNG while Playwright/Chromium renders the body. Pre-existing, not caused by the CSS work: `git diff 4de0fca HEAD -- internal/net internal/download` is empty. Blast radius measured so far is one URL in the 100-site corpus; the shape is common enough (429 challenge pages served with a hand-built header) that the honest description is 'unknown until swept again'. What closing it needs: parameter parsing that splits on ';' and trims, a table-driven oracle in test/download covering `text/html`, `text/html;charset=utf-8`, `text/html; charset=utf-8`, `text/html, charset=UTF-8`, `application/xhtml+xml`, and a genuinely downloadable `application/pdf; charset=binary`; plus a user-visible consequence - a -screenshot run whose answer was routed to the downloader must say so on stderr instead of exiting 1 silently, which is the same class as GOOSIE-LIVE-003 (a run that gave up looks like a run that succeeded).

summary: The parity harness reads and writes two fixed /tmp directories, so two agents or two worktrees running it at the same time score one run's renders against another's - and the collision surfaces as a traceback, not as a refusal.
evidence: GOOSIE = Path('/tmp/goosie-renders') and CHROMIUM = Path('/tmp/playwright-renders') (testdata/parity.py:59-60) are global, unversioned and shared by every checkout on the machine, and --render truncates them in place. Measured at 02:10 on 2026-10-26: while this session's 100-site live sweep and another agent's `make parity` (pid 87939, `testdata/parity.py --render --render-chromium`) were both running, a read-only scoring pass in a third checkout died with `PIL.UnidentifiedImageError: cannot identify image file '/tmp/goosie-renders/grid/02-grid-alignment.png'` - a half-written PNG from the other process, rc 1, no verdict. The crash is the harmless outcome: the same race lets run A's Goosie renders be scored against run B's Chromium references, from different binaries, with nothing in the report saying which build produced either side. TASK-036 already established that a green `make parity` is one host's evidence; this is the same weakness one level down - within one host it is not even one BUILD's evidence. What closing needs: one render directory per run (mkdtemp, or a path derived from the binary's sha256), the chosen directory recorded in the JSON report next to each fixture, and a selftest case that proves two concurrent runs cannot read each other's files. Note the discipline that follows for agents: TASK-042 deliberately ran `python3 testdata/parity.py` without --render to avoid destroying evidence that other work was reading (its rule 9), which is right but invisible - nothing in the harness says the directory is somebody else's evidence.

summary: A document the source refused (4xx) is still rendered and scored as if it were the page, so the live harness labels a blocked site LAYOUT_EMPTY - 'the engine made nothing' and 'the site said no' share one label.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-005. TASK-039 put the refusal on stderr (`goosie: the source refused <url> with HTTP <status>; rendered <n> bytes of that refusal, not the page`, cmd/goosie/document_loader.go:455, oracle BR-190 with mutation M5 re-measured by the integrator: nipping the threshold to `>= 0` kills `TestGoosieScreenshotStaysSilentOnAnAcceptedDocument`). The harness half is not done: testdata/live-parity.py compares whatever Chromium and Goosie each painted and has no field for the HTTP status, so a 403 body scores as LAYOUT_EMPTY or LOW_COVERAGE. Measured in docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1920Z-eef92ae7.json: 8 rows carry LAYOUT_EMPTY, and the sweep's own `goosie_diag` is where the refusal now lives, not in the label. What closing needs: capture the response status per page, add a REFUSED_BY_SOURCE label, and count how many of the current LAYOUT_EMPTY rows are actually refusals - until then the eight-page figure inside GOOSIE-LIVE-001 is an upper bound that mixes two causes.

summary: A 20-32 px ink smudge in the top-left corner of Goosie's renders is counted by content_bands as a content band, so a page whose only Goosie output is that smudge reads as 'has content'.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-006. At ink_goosie=32 the vnexpress.net render (viewport 1280x1024) is a smudge inside (0,0)-(4,3) and nothing else; parity.content_bands treats its row range as a band, and the sweep recorded it as BLANK_OUTPUT only because the coverage ratio collapsed, not because the band was rejected. TASK-039 §5.5 measured what the smudge is (branch F) but did not root-cause which tile produces it, and §5.11.4 records that the probe needed is on the raster/frame side with a minimal fixture. What closing needs: a fixture that paints nothing but the corner, a statement of which of the two (uncovered tile, glyph-atlas bleed) it is, and a floor in the band metric that ignores a band of that size - the floor must be set from measurement, not tuned until the label goes away.

summary: An escaped quote inside an unquoted url() token opens a string that never closes, so every rule after it in the same stylesheet is dropped - the shape that hides vnexpress's tail rules and that the current parser only survives by luck when the sheet holds an even number of quote characters.
evidence: GOOSIE-CSSSTRING-003. CSS Syntax L3 4.3.8 makes a backslash escape the next byte anywhere in the token stream, so `\'` inside `url(...)` must not start a string. Goosie applies the escape-skip only in the `quote != 0` branch of the boundary scanners (internal/css/parser.go, parseRule's selector and declaration loops and parseBlockWithRules' statement loop), so outside a string the `'` of `\'` still opens one. Measured on a minimal file (one `.u{background-image:url(data:image/svg+xml;...\'26\'...)}` rule plus `.after{background:#0f0}` and a text node, viewport 400x300): Chromium computes `.u` width 120px and `.after` rgb(0,255,0) - both rules survive; eef92ae paints 2,806 ink px (both boxes gone, only the text), and da68c5b paints 16,325 (both boxes). This is a REGRESSION introduced by a9f6218, which added the inside-string skip. Second measurement, on vnexpress.net's own second inline <style> block (94,344 bytes, one line, 80 single quotes, 409 backslashes) with a `.ZZ{background:#0f0;width:120px;height:120px}` marker appended: da68c5b paints the marker (14,400 px), eef92ae paints nothing (0 px). The two builds differ only in whether an escaped quote closes a string, so the old one was right by accident - an even number of quote characters leaves the state balanced - and the new one is wrong for that shape. Both directions are real: on the whole vnexpress.net page ink went 32 -> 320,348 between the da68c5b and eef92ae sweeps, because a different sheet on that page has the odd-count shape. Why no gate saw it: no test under test/css contains an escaped quote inside a string or a url token, and BR-186's nine tests cover the raw-newline and escaped-newline halves only; the render corpus has no escaped-quote-in-url fixture, so `make parity` is 83/83 green across this change. What closing needs: the escape-skip in both states at every boundary scanner (including the lenient sites that never end at a newline, parser.go:1321, :1346, :1419, :1681, :1784 and SplitDeclarations), expectations taken from Chromium measurement rather than memory, a unit oracle for `url(...\'...\')`, a parity fixture whose tail rule disappears when the scanner mis-tracks state, and a mutation proof that the fixture kills the current behaviour. CLOSED by e3b8292. Fix: `startsEscape` is tested before the quote branches in every quote-tracking scan (parseRule's selector and body loops, parseBlockWithRules' at-prelude, at-block, statement and nested-rule scans, ExpandSingleNestedSelector, SplitDeclarations), so an escaped byte is consumed with its backslash in both states; the body loop tracks parens apart from braces and 4.3.9 stops a quote inside `url(...)` from opening a string at all. Verified here, not claimed: five oracles green, `go test -count=1 ./...` rc 0, `go vet -all ./...` rc 0, `go test ./internal/archtest/` rc 0, `make parity` 84/84 at average 96.13% with css-features/10 at 97.42% and 0 blank bands, and the gate-level mutation - the same fixture rendered by eef92ae - scores 78.61% FAIL with 5 blank bands and parity exit 1. Re-measured outcomes on the inputs that opened this defect: the marker sheet (vnexpress style#1 + tail rule) paints 14,400 px again instead of 0, and the minimal probe recovers both boxes (16,325 px). Still open, deliberately not folded in: escape *decoding* (Goosie keeps the backslashes in the value while Chromium computes `url("data:x'y")`), hex escapes like `\A`, and selector matching on an escaped quote (GOOSIE-CSSSELECT-001). None of them changes a pixel on the shapes measured here - Chromium computes `background-image: none` for the vnexpress-style URI too - so they stay recorded as debt rather than being fixed blind.

summary: A selector whose quoted value holds an escaped quote parses into the stylesheet but never matches, so the element keeps its unstyled box - the rule exists, the match does not.
evidence: GOOSIE-CSSSELECT-001. Measured 2026-10-26 on `.s[data-x="a\"b"]{background:#8e44ad;height:24px}` with `<div class="s" data-x='a"b'>`: Chromium computes the band 760x24 at rgb(142,68,173); Goosie paints no band at all. This is not the parser losing the rule - test/css/escaped_quote_test.go:TestEscapedQuoteInsideSelectorAttributeKeepsFollowingRules proves the rule and both its declarations survive (that half is BR-191) - so the loss is in selector matching, which still compares the raw text including the backslash. TASK-041 §7.6 already recorded 'selector text keeps the escape pair' as remaining debt; this is that debt with a measured page-level consequence. The render fixture css-features/10-escaped-quote-url.html deliberately uses an unescaped attribute value, so nothing in the corpus enshrines the wrong match. What closing needs: unescape the value when a selector is compiled (CSS Syntax L3 4.3.10 identifiers and 4.3.7 strings), one oracle per side (escaped quote, escaped space, hex escape like `\A`), and a fixture whose band only paints when the match works.
